litigation.note: Long-running competition-law litigation is pending. Appeals before the NCLAT arising from CCI orders on abuse of dominance (delay in FSA execution, faulty pricing mechanism, inferior quality of coal supplied, bank guarantee costs and refunds of performance incentives) involve CIL and subsidiaries MCL, WCL. Matters described include WBPDCL appeal proceedings, Competition Appeal (AT) 36 of 2018 filed by KPCL against CCI's order of 16th March 2018 (with a related consolidation application), and a Section 53N compensation claim by SWPL against WCL/CIL pending before NCLAT and effectively held in abeyance pursuant to the Supreme Court's interim order of 10th April 2018. Amounts are disclosed in the source but are deliberately not reproduced here. Note: the routed Corporate Governance section is truncated, so this is a partial view of disclosed litigation.

risks.note: CIL's near-monopoly on domestic coal is being eroded by captive and commercial miners. It is formally classified as a Risk That Matter and is also shown as a strategic 'Risk to Value Creation' in the value-creation model. Management's stated response is implementation of SHAKTI 2025, enabling imported-coal-based power plants to obtain domestic coal linkages, encouraging wider participation in coal auctions including foreign bidders, and customer-centric measures to enhance market competitiveness - i.e. defending share rather than pricing power.
risks.risk: Business risk from captive and commercial coal mining (Risk That Matter)

risks.note: The energy-transition risk is explicitly on the RTM register: India's climate commitments could structurally cap or reverse coal demand. This is the existential risk for a single-commodity producer whose entire core business is thermal coal, and it is the stated rationale for the renewable, storage, gasification and critical-minerals diversification. The routed text is truncated mid-sentence exactly where management begins describing its response ('CIL continues to').
risks.risk: Impact of Nationally Determined Commitments (NDCs) on coal demand and production (Risk That Matter)

risks.note: Land is the binding constraint on the 1 BT-by-FY30 roadmap: 4,171.79 Ha must be possessed by subsidiaries just to hit the FY 2026-27 target, and land/R&R delays are cited as a primary bottleneck behind 33 of 124 ongoing projects running late. The stated risk explicitly includes the cost consequence of the permanent-employment obligations attached to land acquisition, which converts a project delay into a structural cost burden.
risks.risk: Delay in land acquisition and possession for mining projects, with cost implication for permanent employment (Risk That Matter)

risks.note: Environmental Clearance and Stage-II Forest Clearance gate incremental capacity - EC for 8 proposals of about 21.45 Mty and Stage-II FC for 12 proposals covering 2,800.145 Ha of forest land are required for the FY 2026-27 target alone. Forest Clearance delays are named as a primary bottleneck for delayed projects. Clearance timing is outside the Company's control and directly determines whether production targets are met.
risks.risk: Delay in obtaining statutory clearances (Risk That Matter)

risks.note: Mining is described by management as an inherently complex business where safety remains the foremost priority. It carries both a human cost and the risk of mine stoppages and regulatory action. Mitigation is comprehensive safety audits of all producing mines, Principal Hazard Management Plans, mine-specific Safety Management Plans, Integrated Command and Control Centres across all producing subsidiaries and NEC, AI-enabled video analytics and a Safety AI Analytics Dashboard.

Listed first among the six RTMs and repeated in the SWOT threats and the value-creation risk map. CIL runs SAP as its system of record across mining projects and financial reporting, with an Online Reconciliation Portal integrating quantity, quality and finance data for external consumers, so a cyber event would hit operations, customer settlement and financial reporting simultaneously.

Structurally important because it collides with strategy: opencast mines contributed 96.67% of raw coal output in FY 2025-26 and opencastable coal is stated to be likely exhausted in the near future, forcing a shift to underground mining where a 50 MT-by-2029-30 vision plan and at least 140 Continuous Miners by 2034-35 are planned. Underground capacity utilisation was 77% versus 88% for opencast. The Company itself flags that these operations may be unviable.
risks.risk: Risk of unviable underground mining operations (Non-RTM Major Risk)

risks.note: Named as 'Inadequate Succession Planning leading to shortage of critical manpower' on the risk register and echoed in the SWOT weaknesses as 'ageing work force and skill attrition'. With 2,12,066 employees and a simultaneous need to staff renewable energy, storage and critical-minerals businesses, capability transition is a live constraint; mitigation is training, leadership programmes and lateral hiring.
risks.risk: Critical manpower and succession planning risk (Non-RTM Major Risk)
